paraphrase: Purandara says: 'The Cārvākas too accept inference as it is known in the world; what is rejected is the inference that some state by transgressing the worldly path.' Śāntarakṣita answers that the world too infers causes from effects, and in truth that is all the logicians claim.

original.text: lokaprasiddham anumānaṃ cārvākair apīṣyata eva, yat tu kaiścil laukikaṃ mārgam atikramyānumānam ucyate tan niṣidhyate
original.edition: Tattvasaṅgraha with Pañjikā, SARIT e-text, checked locally
original.licence: ancient text (public domain); e-text consulted read-only for reference

notes: Reported by an opponent: Kamalaśīla (Buddhist), quoting Purandara. Checked in the SARIT e-text.

paraphrase: Kamalaśīla: 'and so their sūtra: in the aggregate of these are the designations object and sense' — for sense-organs and the rest are nothing apart from the great elements, being particular arrangements of them.
notes: Reported by an opponent: Kamalaśīla (Buddhist). Checked; the sūtra is also quoted by Jayarāśi in a different word order.

paraphrase: Kamalaśīla: 'and so the sūtra — from the body alone' (kāyād eva): Kambalāśvatara's statement that cognition comes from the body sustained by the breaths.
notes: Reported by an opponent: Kamalaśīla (Buddhist). Checked.
